title: [PDF] The Basel Framework - Bank for International Settlements
summary: The Basel Framework is the comprehensive compilation of all standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), the primary global standard setter for prudential bank regulation. This 1982-page PDF document covers capital definitions, risk-based capital requirements, credit risk approaches, market risk frameworks, operational risk, leverage ratios, and other prudential standards that internationally active banks must implement. Note: The specific publication date of this framework version is not stated in the document.
key_points: BCBS sets global prudential standards for internationally active banks across member jurisdictions
Framework includes capital definition standards (CAP), risk-based capital requirements (RBC), and credit risk approaches (CRE)
Market risk calculation standards (MAR) cover both standardised approach and internal models approach
Operational risk (OPE) and leverage ratio (LEV) requirements are fully documented
Framework includes specific provisions for cryptoasset exposures (SCO60)
Global and domestic systemically important bank (G-SIB/D-SIB) buffers are defined
why_it_matters: This is the foundational regulatory reference for global bank capital and risk standards. While not a specific policy announcement, it defines the rules that govern bank capital requirements, risk weighting methodologies, and market risk calculations—all of which affect how banks allocate capital and the cost of market-making activities.
macro_context: The Basel Framework provides the regulatory architecture that shapes bank behavior globally. Key sections cover: banking book vs trading book boundaries; standardised and internal models approaches for market risk; counterparty credit risk frameworks; and capital treatment for securities financing transactions.
market_structure_context: This framework document defines the regulatory architecture for bank capital requirements and market risk calculations globally. Key sections cover: boundary between banking book and trading book; standardised approach for market risk; internal models methodology; counterparty credit risk; and capital treatment of securities financing transactions. These standards directly influence bank behavior in market-making, derivatives intermediation, and securities financing markets.
important_numbers: Multiple standard modules: SCO (Scope), CAP (Capital), RBC (Risk-based capital), CRE (Credit risk), MAR (Market risk), OPE (Operational risk), LEV (Leverage)
